local.headline: County Commission advances data center rules; MLGW proposes gas and water rate hikes
body: Action News 5 reported that the Shelby County Commission took up its own data center rules, with a little over 100 days left on the Memphis City Council's moratorium. The proposal passed first reading, 9 to 4, and needs two more readings. It would change zoning options, set noise limits and outline water use. Supporters of the rules back them, while some business leaders oppose limits and call data centers an economic engine.

Action News 5 also reported that Memphis Light, Gas and Water wants its first gas and water rate increases since 2022, phased in over three years and subject to City Council approval. The station put the added cost at $10 a month for water and $18 a month for gas. MLGW CEO Doug McGowen said there is never a good time to raise rates. Councilman JB Smiley said MLGW should draw on its reserve fund, which the utility says it can no longer rely on.

state.headline: Tennessee flu activity rated high; steady rain expected for Wednesday travel
body: FOX13 Memphis reported that the CDC's latest flu map puts Tennessee in the "high" activity category, while Arkansas and Mississippi are at "moderate." Dr. Chinelo Animalu of Methodist Le Bonheur Healthcare said she is seeing more flu patients, that the season started earlier than usual, and that influenza A is far more common than influenza B. She said it is not too late to get vaccinated, though protection takes about two weeks to build.

WSMV reported that Wednesday is a First Alert Weather Day for Middle Tennessee, with widespread rain expected to disrupt holiday travel. The rain is forecast to start in the morning near the Tennessee River and reach the I-65 corridor around the evening rush, steady and at times heavy. WSMV advised drivers to leave early and said some areas could see light snow on Thanksgiving Day.

federal.headline: Nvidia reinstates CEO Jensen Huang after Trump push; Iowa explosives burn on hold
body: CBS News reported that Nvidia's board said Monday it reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, less than two weeks after he resigned. The board said it received input from senior U.S. officials and sees no national security risk. President Trump told PBS NewsHour that Huang "did absolutely nothing wrong." Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries called the decision "indefensible," and ABC News reported that several Republican senators also criticized it. Huang is scheduled to testify publicly before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 3.

CBS News and PBS NewsHour reported that Trump told the Army to hold off on detonating about 9,500 pounds of degraded lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. Trump said he was deferring to the 8th Circuit appeals court and Iowa's incoming governor, Rob Sand. A federal appeals court had temporarily suspended the Army's permit for the work.

international.headline: Iran vows to counter US blockade; UN chief urges talks on AI safety framework
body: CBS News reported that Iran's foreign ministry spokesman, Esmaeil Baqaei, said Iran would use "all available means" to counter the U.S. naval blockade of its ports. ABC News reported that talks remain stalled and that Iran claims control of the Strait of Hormuz. CBS News said Iran's navy reported that three oil tankers hit naval mines in the strait on Monday, with no casualties reported at first. President Trump posted that Iran launched more drones and missiles this past week than in over a year, and that they were shot down with no damage.

UN News reported that Secretary-General António Guterres, speaking Monday at an AI safety summit in Barbados, urged member states to begin talks on a multilateral AI risk framework. It would cover shared safety measures, testing, transparency and independent evaluation of advanced models. He described AI as shifting power from governments to a small number of companies and people.
